turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select 5 candidates
that jointly span the best trade-off between a LARGE SHG tensor component
|d_ij| and a WIDE band gap. Neither is given for the pool. Your 5 picks are
scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the normalized (|d_ij|,
band gap) plane, so a set of mutually non-dominated candidates covering the
frontier beats 5 candidates that are all strong on the same single axis.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from structure to (SHG, gap) trade-off

**Screening logic.** SHG requires a non-centrosymmetric (NCS) lattice; |d_ij| is maximized by dense networks of aligned, highly polarizable covalent tetrahedra (P/Se/Te-based, d⁰/d¹⁰ cations), while wide gaps come from more ionic, lighter-anion frameworks (S, halides, Be/Li/Al). The best frontier set staggers picks along this trade-off.

**High-SHG anchor — c030 (CdSiP₂).** Chalcopyrite I-42d, the benchmark IR NLO crystal: fully aligned CdP₄/SiP₄ tetrahedra give a huge d₃₆ (~80–90 pm/V) with a still-usable ~2.4 eV gap. Nothing else in the pool beats it on |d|.

**Strong-SHG / mid-gap — c006 (KBa₃Ga₅Se₁₀Cl₂).** Member of the known ABa₃Ga₅Se₁₀Cl₂ NLO family (polar Cc): a corner-linked [Ga₅Se₁₀] supertetrahedral framework with charge-balancing Ba/Cl. AgGaS₂-class SHG with a ~3.0 eV gap — an excellent middle frontier point.

**Balanced — c075 (Cu₄AlGaS₈ ≈ CuAl₀.₅Ga₀.₅S₂).** Ordered chalcopyrite-type Cu(Al,Ga)S₂: aligned CuS₄/(Al,Ga)S₄ tetrahedra, d₃₆ ~10–15 pm/V, gap ~3.3–3.5 eV (between CuGaS₂ and CuAlS₂).

**Wide gap with real SHG — c057 (LiAlS₂).** β-NaFeO₂/wurtzite-derived Pna₂₁ structure — guaranteed polar, all LiS₄/AlS₄ tetrahedra co-aligned. Light, ionic constituents push the gap to ~4–4.4 eV while retaining a modest but nonzero d (LiMX₂ family behavior, high laser-damage threshold).

**Widest gap end — c037 (BeSe, zinc-blende F-4̄3m).** Guaranteed NCS (d₁₄ allowed), very strong Be–Se covalent tetrahedra, and a wide ~4.5–5.5 eV gap — dominates halide picks (BaBrCl, Rb₄OCl₂) whose SHG would be nearly zero and thus add almost no hypervolume.

These five are mutually non-dominated: |d| decreases monotonically (≈85 → ~25 → ~12 → ~2–5 → small) as the gap rises (2.4 → 3.0 → 3.4 → ~4.2 → ~5 eV), covering the whole frontier rather than clustering on one axis.

Final: c030, c006, c075, c057, c037
